centre.source: SIMBAD basic.ra/dec for M31 (oid 1575544), position bibcode 2006AJ....131.1163S (2MASS)

quote: Considering the galaxy disk between 10 and 25 kpc with an average inclination of 77.7° and position angle 38°
choice: One flat plane from Corbelli et al. (2010), a joint tilted-ring fit of the H I velocity field. Its 10-25 kpc range holds the 10 kpc star-forming ring, where most of the HII regions, Cepheids and young clusters lie, and its inclination agrees with the stellar-disc measurement below. The same paper also calls the inner-disk values i = 77.6°, θ = 38° (Sect. 2); the 0.1° difference is recorded, not resolved.

crossChecks.tracer: Stellar disc: maximum fraction of reddened stars plus the old disc's axial ratio, allowing for its thickness.
crossChecks.agreement: Inclination within 0.7° of the adopted value. The paper gives no position angle.

crossChecks.tracer: H I tilted rings from DRAO data.
crossChecks.agreement: Position angle agrees; inclination 3.4° lower. Corbelli et al. (2010, Sect. 2.2) discuss the difference and find their 77° closer to optical surface photometry.

crossChecks.tracer: Old red-giant disc in the PHAT footprint (north-east third of the disc).
crossChecks.agreement: Position angle 6.4° higher. The paper reports it as 6-8° off the H I disc at 5-20 kpc and notes that older, heated populations can look more face-on than the younger disc, so it is not used for young tracers.

limits: A single plane. The disc warps: Corbelli et al. (2010, Table 1) fit inclinations from 75.1° to 78.6° inside 25 kpc and up to 86° beyond 30 kpc, and Chemin et al. (2009) find the inner 6 kpc less inclined. Dots placed on this plane inherit that error, largest for the outer planetary nebulae.
